items.title: Microsoft Research releases TokenEconomizer for more efficient AI coding agents
items.summary_en: Microsoft Research describes an open-source plugin that lets AI coding agents reuse lessons from earlier sessions. The stated aim is to lower agent token costs while keeping task success high.
items.notes: Taken from the fetched blog listing page (title, date, one-line description). The individual post was not opened, so no results or numbers are reported.

items.title: Microsoft Research describes 'Lazarus' backdoor that reprograms dormant neurons in AI agents
items.summary_en: Researchers present an attack in which dormant neurons are reprogrammed so that an AI agent runs malicious commands when a hidden trigger appears. The post falls under AI agent security research.
items.notes: Taken from the blog listing page only. Published 2026-11-10, one day before the nominal 10-day window; included because it is the latest agent-security item from this target. Details of the method and any mitigations were not read.

items.title: Microsoft Ignite 2026 (Nov 17-20): Copilot as work layer, Agent 365, models, transparency initiative
items.summary_en: Search coverage of Ignite 2026, which opened on November 17, describes Microsoft positioning Copilot as a work operating system or intelligence layer. Reported announcements include Agent 365 business analytics (via the Frontier early-access program), Copilot Workspaces, GPT-6.2 series models generally available on Microsoft Foundry, and MAI Licensed Weights for deploying and customizing MAI models in a customer's Azure environment. Also reported are an AI Transparency Initiative with more than 40 partners, HorizonDB (distributed PostgreSQL) GA, and Cobalt 200 VMs.
items.source_name: Microsoft News Source Asia (official Microsoft newsroom)
items.notes: The official newsroom URL appeared in search results, but news.microsoft.com and blogs.microsoft.com did not resolve from this session, so the page was not read. The product details come from a search-engine summary that drew on several third-party outlets. Individual product claims (for example MAI Licensed Weights, the AI Transparency Initiative, GPT-6.2 GA, the Microsoft Perception defense system) are unverified against Microsoft's own posts and should be checked before use. The publication date is taken from the URL path. Reports note that Frontier is early access and that GA does not mean rollout is complete everywhere.

coverage_note: Microsoft Research blog listing was read directly. Its two posts in the window are dated Nov 10 and Nov 16, 2026, and the next most recent are Nov 5 and Oct 30. The official Microsoft AI blog (blogs.microsoft.com/ai) and news.microsoft.com could not be fetched, because those hosts are not in the session's allowed network domains and need to be allowed in the session's network settings. As a result, Ignite 2026 (Nov 17-20) coverage rests on search snippets and is marked primary-inferred. No official social accounts, interview transcripts or talk recordings were checked. Other Microsoft Research posts such as PDD Kit (Nov 5), Copilot synthetic-data evaluation (Oct 30) and the KLS conjecture (Oct 21) fall outside the window and are omitted. No third-party items were created.
